title: 31 Metabolomic analysis of boar seminal plasma identifies sperm-quality related metabolites
content:
Abstract
Predicting the reproductive potential of boars remains a significant challenge for the swine industry, where breeding largely relies on artificial insemination to improve reproductive efficiency. Therefore, understanding the molecular mechanism of seminal plasma (SP) and its role in male fertility is essential for gaining insights into sperm physiology of boars with varying fertility levels. Seminal plasma, the primary medium for sperm, is rich in diverse biomolecules, including metabolites that can influence sperm function. However, metabolic signatures related to boar semen quality remain unknown. This study aimed to identify metabolites in boar seminal plasma derived from Passed (high-quality) and Failed (low-quality) semen samples and to elucidate the molecular pathways that may influence sperm function. Semen samples (n=64) were collected from sexually mature Duroc boars at a commercial boar stud (Prestage Farms, West Point, MS). Semen samples were classified as Passed (>70% motility and morphology, with mean+SD) and Failed (< 70% motility and morphology, with mean-SD) based on predefined criteria. SP was isolated from five selected samples per semen group through centrifugation for metabolomics analysis. Untargeted metabolomics was performed using Ultra-High Performance Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (UHPLC-MS). Significant metabolites were identified based on Variable Importance in Projection (VIP > 1.5) and a significance level of P < 0.05. Furthermore, metabolic pathway enrichment analysis was conducted using the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) database and MetaboAnalyst to visualize key metabolic networks. Multivariate statistical analysis revealed distinct metabolic profiles between the Passed and Failed SP samples. A total of 373 metabolites in the positive and 478 metabolites in the negative ion modes were detected. Among these, eleven differentially expressed metabolites (DEMs) were identified. Nine DEMs, including indole-3-acetamide, dopamine, glutamine lactate, metanephrine, betaine, allopurinol, formycin B, stearoylcarnitine, and lysoPC were upregulated in the Passed samples. In contrast, cyclopentylamine and tyrosine were downregulated. These DEMs may serve as potential biomarkers of semen quality, contributing to sperm membrane integrity, energy metabolism, oxidative stress regulation, motility, and overall fertilizing ability. Additionally, KEGG pathway analysis revealed significant enrichment in glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, tyrosine metabolism, and the biosynthesis of phenylalanine. In conclusion, this study provides valuable insights into boar seminal plasma metabolites associated with semen quality. These findings have the potential to improve semen assessment techniques, ultimately enhancing male reproductive performance in swine production systems.
